The maintenance report lists the files changed, owners added or moved and the checker result.

Verification starts with the final changed-file set and diff: the change matches the requested scope without unrelated refactoring, no generated or build artifacts or secrets were added, and temporary probes are removed only after preservation.

After all fixes the final diff is reviewed for unrelated edits, commented-out code, temporary logging, TODO/FIXME markers, stale temporary tests or scripts, architecture drift, unapproved product drift and stale surfaces after a settings change.
Do not use --no-restore unless restore is known to be complete.
For small solutions run the complete test suite; for large solutions run affected test projects first, then broader suites as required.
Build the affected projects; a solution that does not build is not complete (never report successful scaffolding for it).
Run the relevant tests.
All files use UTF-8, space indentation, a final newline and trimmed trailing whitespace, except that Markdown keeps trailing whitespace.
Indent 2 spaces for JSON/YAML, project/XML and TS/JS/HTML/SCSS/CSS files (single quotes for TS/JS) and 4 spaces for C#.
Interfaces must begin with I (warning severity).
Fields, properties, methods and events are not qualified with this.
Async methods are expected to end with Async, but detection only covers async-modified methods and no framework/interface contract exemption is encoded.
var is suggested when the type is apparent; explicit types elsewhere are allowed.
SPECIFICATION.md and CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md must not contradict each other; on an apparent conflict stop and ask which source must be corrected rather than choosing one.
Resolve a conflict between SPECIFICATION.md and CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md before changing implementation.

Do not silently invent a value that materially changes accepted input or observable behavior when no product source defines it: propose it with its reason, ask for approval, record it in CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md and synchronize it through custom-settings.
Undefined tunable values are a Reserved decision.
Do not introduce CQRS handlers, MediatR, Kommand, Vertical Slice Architecture or similar mediator-based organization unless explicitly approved.
The manifest check notes a MediatR reference as requiring an approved decision.
NgRx, Axios, Lodash, Bootstrap, Tailwind and additional form, component or state-management libraries are not added by default; an extra library is added only for a concrete need.
The manifest check notes these packages.
Changing an accepted project or architecture decision is Reserved (explicit approval unless already required by the specification or established structure).
A new architectural style or pattern (Rich Domain Model or DDD tactical patterns, CQRS/MediatR/Vertical Slice Architecture, event sourcing, microservices) is Reserved.
A new production project, layer or assembly or an additional DbContext/persistence boundary is Reserved.
Changed persistence boundaries or persistence technology are Reserved.
A new messaging, background-processing or distributed-caching infrastructure category is Reserved.
A new search, external-storage or external-identity infrastructure category is Reserved.
A major library or framework is Reserved.
Replacing an approved baseline technology is Reserved.
A project-wide convention or abstraction other code must follow (e.g. a project-wide Result model) is Reserved.
A new or changed authentication/authorization architecture is Reserved.
A breaking public API change is Reserved.
A changed project reference graph is Reserved.
A project-wide convention or abstraction other code must follow is Reserved.
Adopting API versioning is Reserved.

In an unclear case any 'yes' to the five questions (dependency/framework/infrastructure add-remove-replace, boundary change, new convention, observable behavior or contract change, expensive to reverse) makes the decision Reserved.
Do not commit, push, merge, rebase, reset, force-push, delete branches or perform other repository-changing Git operations unless explicitly requested.
Completing an implementation is not a request to commit, push, merge or rewrite history.
Nullable reference types are enabled for every project.
Implicit global usings are enabled for every project.
.NET analyzers run at AnalysisLevel latest for every project.
EditorConfig code-style diagnostics are enforced during build.
The backend platform is .NET 10 LTS, C# 14, ASP.NET Core and ASP.NET Core Controllers; moving to a preview/RC .NET or C# release requires approval.
.NET 10 is used on its latest stable servicing release.
FluentValidation is the standard library for explicit request and use-case validation.
Application code logs through ILogger<T> with Serilog (Serilog.AspNetCore) as the provider.
Serilog sinks are added only when required.
Do not use a deprecated or legacy ASP.NET automatic-validation integration package without a concrete requirement.
Add Serilog sinks only when required; a Console sink is enough for local Development.
Testing uses NUnit; Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing with WebApplicationFactory<Program> is the integration-test baseline; backend test projects live under backend/ beside the production projects.
Testcontainers is used only when isolated real-provider tests justify it.

Angular baseline: the latest stable release supported by the selected Node.js, created with the current Angular CLI (compatible TypeScript and RxJS), standalone APIs, strict mode, routing, zoneless when supported, SCSS, Angular Material and CDK, Vitest.
No TypeScript upgrade beyond Angular's supported range and no obsolete directory structure imposed over the CLI's.
Conditional technologies are added only when their capability is needed.
Manual mapping for simple cases, Mapster when mapping volume warrants it, and no other mapping framework without approval.
The Microsoft resilience packages are added only when a real integration needs resilience.
